question: Which of the following plants can have buds in the margins of leaves?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bryophyllum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bryophyllum** is a genus of plant species that belongs to the **Crassulaceae** family. It is widely recognized for its unique method of **asexual reproduction**.
 
• The leaves of **Bryophyllum** are broad and have **notches** along their **margins**. These notches contain specialized tissue that develops into **adventitious buds**.
 
• These **buds** are also known as **epiphyllous buds**. When a leaf matures or falls onto **moist soil**, these buds develop into small **plantlets** with their own roots and stems.
 
• Once the plantlets are sufficiently developed, they detach from the parent leaf and grow into independent **new plants**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Bryophyllum.***
 
• This process allows the plant to multiply rapidly without the immediate need for **seeds** or **pollination**, ensuring survival in various environmental conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• It is a form of **asexual reproduction** in plants where new individuals arise from **vegetative parts** like **roots, stems, or leaves** rather than from **seeds**.
 
• In **natural vegetative propagation**, plants use structures like **runners** (strawberry), **tubers** (potato), **bulbs** (onion), and **leaf buds** (Bryophyllum).
 
 
 
• **Mango (Mangifera indica):**
 
 
• **Mango** is a **dicotyledonous** plant that primarily reproduces sexually through **seeds**.
 
• In agriculture, it is often propagated through **artificial vegetative methods** like **grafting** to maintain specific fruit qualities, but it does not produce buds on its **leaf margins**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Neem (Azadirachta indica):**
 
 
• **Neem** belongs to the **Meliaceae** family and is native to the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• It reproduces mainly through **seeds** (neem beans) and occasionally through **root suckers**. Its leaves are used for **medicinal purposes** but do not have reproductive buds. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Peepal (Ficus religiosa):**
 
 
• The **Peepal** tree, or **Sacred Fig**, is known for its **cordate-shaped** leaves with a long **distal tip**.
 
• It reproduces via **seeds**, which are often dispersed by birds. While it is a hardy tree that can grow in **crevices** of walls, it does not utilize its leaf margins for **budding**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Begonia** is another common example of a plant that can produce **buds** on its **leaves** for the purpose of **vegetative propagation**.
 
• The **adventitious buds** in **Bryophyllum** are formed due to the presence of **meristematic tissue** at the edges of the leaf.
 
• **Vegetative propagation** is advantageous because the offspring are **genetically identical** to the parent, and it allows for faster growth compared to plants grown from **seeds**.
 
• The **Bryophyllum** plant is often colloquially called the **"Air Plant"** or **"Miracle Leaf"** due to its ability to sprout from detached leaves.
